q: When is a month's GSTR-2B generated?
options: On the 11th of the next month
On the 14th of the next month
On the 20th of the next month
exp: It's a fixed statement. Since IMS, it can be recomputed after IMS actions until 3B is filed.

q: Which of these does NOT feed into GSTR-2B?
options: Bills of entry for imports, from ICEGATE
exp: 2B only shows what others reported. Reconciling it with the purchase register is the recipient's job.

q: Unlike GSTR-2A, GSTR-2B doesn't change when a supplier files late after it's generated.
exp: A late-filed invoice lands in the next 2B instead. Recomputing after IMS actions is the only change allowed.

q: Since 1 January 2022, what's the key link between ITC and GSTR-2B?
options: ITC can be claimed only if the invoice appears in GSTR-2B
ITC can be claimed up to 105% of 2B
exp: The old provisional 5% margin is gone. Section 16(2)(aa) ties the claim to what the supplier reported.
ref: CGST Act, s.16(2)(aa); CGST Rules, r.36(4)

q: A Delhi-registered client's GSTR-2B shows a Mumbai hotel's invoice with CGST and SGST under 'ITC not available'. Why?
options: The place of supply is Maharashtra, so Maharashtra's CGST and SGST can't be claimed by a Delhi registration
exp: For hotel stays the place of supply is where the property is. Asking the hotel to charge IGST isn't the fix.

q: In IMS, what happens to a supplier invoice the client takes no action on by the time 2B is generated?
options: It's deemed accepted and shows as ITC available in 2B
exp: That's why CAs review IMS before the 14th rather than letting everything flow through.

q: A client rejects a supplier's ₹50,000 credit note in IMS because the goods were never returned. What's the effect?
options: Nothing, credit notes can't be rejected
The client's ITC isn't reduced for it, and the tax the credit note had knocked off the supplier's liability is added back
exp: The supplier then has to sort it out with the buyer or pay the tax.

q: Mid-month, a client's IMS shows 300 supplier invoices. The finance head asks why the CA wants to review them before the 14th instead of letting them flow into 2B. Explain.
model: Anything left without action is deemed accepted when 2B is generated, so credit on invoices the client never received, duplicates, invoices meant for another GSTIN or ineligible credits would all show as available. The CA matches IMS against the purchase register: accept what matches, reject what isn't the client's or is wrong so the supplier has to correct it, and keep pending the invoices where goods haven't arrived so the ITC is taken in the right month. Wrong claims lead to reversal with interest and rule 88D intimations. If actions change after the 14th, 2B can be recomputed before filing 3B.
points: Match IMS against the purchase register
Reject wrong invoices and keep undelivered ones pending
exp: IMS turns the monthly ITC review into an up-front step instead of an after-the-fact reconciliation.

q: A supplier's July invoice for ₹2 lakh + ₹36,000 GST shows up only in the client's September 2B because the supplier filed late. When can the client claim it?
options: In September's 3B, when it appears in 2B
exp: ITC follows 2B. It's still inside the s.16(4) time limit for that year, which is 30 November after the year ends.

q: A client imports goods and pays ₹1.8 lakh IGST at customs. Where does it check that the credit is available?
options: The import section (IMPG) of GSTR-2B, fed from bill of entry data on ICEGATE
exp: It's claimed in 3B Table 4(A)(1). A missing bill of entry is usually a GSTIN mismatch on the bill of entry itself.
